source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.6.1 Properties of Trees (PDF 106-108, printed 103-105), as printed: the family tree program as printed with its errors marked, the corrected program in the Book correction, and Figure 4.6.

items: Root Node: The root is the very first or top node in a tree, like the main folder in a computer where all other folders and files are contained.

Edges and Nodes: Nodes are the individual elements in the tree, and they are connected by lines called edges. A node without any child nodes is called a leaf, similar to a file in a folder that doesn't contain any other files.
Height: The height of a tree is the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf. It tells us how deep or tall the tree is.
Balanced Trees: A tree is considered balanced if the branches on the left and right sides are nearly the same height. See the details in Section 4.1.7

blocks.text: Here's a simple example of how to create a family tree structure in Python using classes. This implementation shows how to create family members (nodes) and how to add children (descendants) to them.

blocks.text: As printed this program does not run: Python stops with SyntaxError: invalid character '•' (U+2022) before it reaches the other errors. The listing has: Fami1yMember for FamilyMember; _ _init_ _ for __init__; two statements on one line (self.name = name self.children = []); FamilyTre e for FamilyTree; the names ancestor_name and child_name broken by spaces; a missing ) after parent_name; current.member for current_member; wrong indentation (return result must be inside if result:, and _find_member, its for loop and return None must line up with the other parts of the class); a bullet • for the comment sign #; curly quotes ’ for straight quotes; Parenti and Childl for Parent1 and Child1; and two add_child calls on one line. The program as it should be printed is given below; it builds the tree of Figure 4.6.

blocks.caption: Book correction: the family tree program written correctly

items: The 'FamilyMember' class represents a single person in the family tree. Each person has a name and can have children (descendants).
The 'FamilyTree' class manages the entire tree, starting with an ancestor at the root. It includes functions to add children and find family members.
